name: port-expose-guard
title: Port Expose Guard
description: Port mapping check for docker run, compose and Kubernetes Services that says who can reach each port and flags databases on 0.0.0.0 (which Docker opens ahead of ufw), host networking, -P, NodePort or public LoadBalancers, wrong container ports and unquoted 22:22 YAML, with fixes.

meta.stops: Helps prevent a database port being opened to the internet
meta.summary: Reads docker run, compose ports or a Kubernetes Service back as who can reach each port, so a database isn't published to the internet by accident.
meta.server: Enforce network policy and firewalls at the host or cloud level; never rely on a config review alone.
catches: Database or admin ports bound to every interface
Host networking, -P, NodePort or public LoadBalancer for internal services
Container port the image doesn't listen on (5432:5433)
Unquoted 22:22 that YAML 1.1 reads as a number
On Docker older than 28, 127.0.0.1 binds reachable from the LAN
limits: Reads the config you paste; it can't see cloud security groups or host firewalls
${VAR} binds without defaults can't be judged until run time
Sensitive-port list is a default; pass your own
a11y: Visible label; textarea is described by the readback
Announcements go to a polite live region
Reach is shown as text with icons aria-hidden; focus moves to the first fix

sources.label: Docker: Packet filtering and firewalls (Docker and ufw)

rules.note: Informational. Confirmed: before 28.0.0, hosts on the same L2 segment can reach ports published to localhost; Docker's rules divert traffic before ufw. The YAML 1.1 sexagesimal reading was not re-checked.
